title: The Joy of Sulking
note: When sulking has made union sweeter, she and he each delight in the sulking.

couplets.plain: He has done nothing wrong, yet sulking is what draws out his tenderness.
couplets.pm: He has no fault, but the tenderness he shows me makes me sulk. He gives such boundless joy that I think others may receive this tenderness too, and I can’t bear it.
couplets.note: The Tamil can go either way. The plain reading says sulking draws out his tenderness. Parimelazhagar says his tenderness makes her jealous, and that causes the sulk.
couplets.context: She has been sulking without cause. Her friend asks why, and she answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: sulking is what draws out his tenderness

couplets.plain: The small hurt of sulking may dim his tenderness for a moment, but it comes back greater.
couplets.pm: The small distress of sulking may make his tenderness wilt, but it then gains greatness. A sulk with no real fault behind it soon ends, so the pain doesn’t last, and great joy follows.
couplets.context: Her friend asks why she suffers by sulking, when she could have his tenderness anyway.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Counts the small hurt of sulking as worth it, since his tenderness comes back greater.

couplets.plain: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel, between two people as blended as earth and water?
couplets.pm: Is there any heaven that gives us as much joy as sulking with a lover who is one with us, as water blends with earth? Water takes on the nature of its land, and a lover takes on the nature of the woman he joins, so sulking arises, and great joy follows.
couplets.context: She goes on, to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel

couplets.plain: In the very quarrel that keeps me clinging to him is the weapon that breaks my resolve.
couplets.pm: In the sulking that makes me hold him and not let go lies the weapon that destroys my heart’s resolve. The weapon is his bowing and his pleading words.
couplets.context: Someone asks her how this sulking will end.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: is the weapon that breaks my resolve
links.reason: The quarrel carries its own undoing: inside it is the weapon that breaks her resolve.

couplets.plain: Even when you have done nothing wrong, being kept from the soft shoulders of the one you love has a pleasure of its own.
couplets.pm: Men with no fault, sulked at as though they had one, can’t reach the soft shoulders they love. Even then they find a pleasure too great to name.
couplets.context: He has made up with her and, overjoyed, says this to himself.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: being kept from the soft shoulders of the one you love has a pleasure of its own
links.reason: Being kept from her soft shoulders is the sulk’s gesture, and even the innocent party finds pleasure in it.

couplets.plain: Digesting a meal is sweeter than eating more. In desire, a quarrel is sweeter than making love.
couplets.pm: Digesting what you have eaten is more pleasant than eating more. In desire, a quarrel over an earlier fault is more pleasant than more union. Hunger makes food better, and time apart makes union sweeter.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: a quarrel is sweeter than making love

couplets.plain: In a lovers’ quarrel, the one who loses has won. You see it when you come back together.
couplets.pm: Of the two lovers, the one who gives way in the quarrel is the winner. This isn’t clear at the time, but it shows later in their lovemaking. I gave way then, so now I have had great joy.
couplets.note: The site keeps this couplet out of Reflect, because it could reach someone pressured to give in.
couplets.speaker: he
couplets.sensitive: counsel to yield first could reach someone pressured to give in

links.quote: the one who loses has won
links.reason: Settles who comes out ahead in a lovers’ quarrel: the one who loses has won.

couplets.plain: Will a quarrel bring back the sweetness of our lovemaking, the kind that left her forehead damp with sweat?
couplets.pm: Can I, by her sulking once more, have again the sweetness of the lovemaking that made her forehead sweat?
couplets.note: உப்பு is literally salt, and he reads it as sweetness. The plain reading follows him.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Will a quarrel bring back the sweetness of our lovemaking
links.reason: Hopes another quarrel will bring back the sweetness of their lovemaking.

couplets.plain: Let her go on sulking, this woman in bright jewels, and let the night run on while I plead.
couplets.pm: Let her of the bright jewels sulk with me more, and let this night not dawn, so that there is time for her sulking and my pleading. The quarrel is enough, even better than union.
couplets.speaker: he

links.reason: He wants more of her sulking, and is in no hurry for it to end.

links.quote: let the night run on while I plead

couplets.plain: Sulking is the joy of desire, and the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it, if you get that far.
couplets.pm: Sulking is the joy of desire. The joy of sulking is the embrace, if you can judge the measure, let go and come together. Held too long it brings pain, and ended too soon it brings no pleasure. That balance is hard, which is why he says “if”.
couplets.speaker: he

links.quote: Sulking is the joy of desire
links.reason: The book’s last word on the sulk: it is the joy of desire.

links.quote: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it

ideaLinks.quote: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it
